hypothesis: Hidden (unmapped) faults concentrate in the step-over geometry of the mapped catalogue: breaching links and en echelon strands inside same-dip relay ramps (W 0.1-15 km, |L| <= 3.5 W), N-NE dilational faults inside strike-slip releasing steps, and splays / transfer links at strike-slip terminations; dots placed only inside the best-scored corridors recover withheld faults better than the same pipeline without corridor priors.
mechanism: Relay ramps between overlapping same-dip normal faults are breached by minor oblique and en echelon faults as displacement transfers (Peacock & Sanderson 1994; Giddens & Faulds 2025: ~70% of >120 C step-overs hard-linked); releasing steps and dextral terminations open N-NE normal faults under WNW extension (Faulds et al. 2026). Regional compilations draw these zones as disconnected strands, so the linking faults are what a lidar-based panel could add.
non_fault_mimic: Lithologic and depositional edges that line up across step-overs: pluvial-lake shorelines and alluvial-fan heads in the lidar scarp channel; buried basement relief and intrusive contacts producing gravity / magnetic edges and tilt zero-crossings without faulting; hydrothermally altered but unfaulted volcanic units producing magnetic lows.

dip_inference.rule: hanging wall = lower mean DEM at 600 m and 1.2 km offsets (normal-fault polarity)

dot_overlap_firings_diagnostic.rule: a firing is 'non-discriminating' when random 2-px Poisson dots placed in the same candidate band (same count) already exceed the 70% limit against that raster: the rule then fires for any candidate in the band and cannot separate lane drift from domain overlap. excess_over_random measures genuine similarity.

registry_uniqueness.template_gap_reported: gems57.uniqueness.representation_class classifies registry rasters by support fraction only; a uniform 6-px lattice (r14_union_tips10_lat6, 3.7% support) covers ~76% of the allowed domain within 3 px and fires the 70% rule for any candidate. Proposed template fix: also classify by 3-px halo coverage of the allowed domain and test each firing against random dots placed in the candidate's own domain (if random dots also exceed 0.70 the firing is non-discriminating). Not edited locally (no private fork).
registry_uniqueness.decision_rule: surface phase: Spearman > 0.90 vs any raster; dots phase: Spearman > 0.90 vs any raster or > 70% of dots within 3 px of one dot-field raster's dots (support <= 20% of footprint). Literal overlap vs continuous surfaces reported as degenerate diagnostics.
